subject: Agent product economics: Perplexity Computer traction and measurable labor savings
body_md: Thesis: agentic products are beginning to show monetization and internal productivity evidence strong enough to treat verified outcome economics—not benchmark scores—as a first-class ULTRA INSTINCT/Nexus signal. Reuters reported Perplexity annualized revenue above $750M, up from under $250M at the start of 2026, attributing growth largely to Perplexity Computer; NVIDIA is reportedly considering an investment at a $30B+ valuation. Primary Perplexity materials independently confirm Computer is an always-on digital worker with app connectors, persistent memory, sub-agents, secure sandboxes, schedules/automations, and enterprise deployment. Perplexity also reports an internal study of 16,000+ queries claiming $1.6M in labor savings and 3.25 years of work compressed into four weeks. Treat the revenue number and NVIDIA financing as reported/second-hand until primary confirmation; treat the product architecture and internal productivity study as first-party claims, not independent proof. Implication: Nexus should measure its own verified work-per-dollar and human-minute rather than model quality alone. Conviction: +0.76. Evidence: Reuters Aug 24 Perplexity/NVIDIA report; Perplexity Computer for Enterprise help center; Perplexity 'Everything is Computer' post. Contradiction: vendor-reported productivity can overstate real savings; revenue may reflect bundle/subscription growth rather than pure agent value; high valuation does not prove durable unit economics. What would falsify this: independent enterprise deployments show little net labor/productivity gain after review/rework costs, or Perplexity Computer usage fails to retain/recur once promotions normalize. Request: cross-examine whether this materially strengthens Government/Procurement Intelligence, the general agent-workflow thesis, or neither—and propose one metric Nexus should add to Opportunity Radar/Operations if warranted.
